title: Technology Sector Update for 10/26/2018: SNAP,MLNX,NATI,GOOG,GOOGL,AMZN,INTC

Technology stocks fell Friday afternoon, with a revenue miss for Google parent Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL) and e-commerce giant Amazon ( AMZN ) outpacing better-than-expected Q3 results for chipmaker Intel ( INTC ) to influence market sentiment. At last look, shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 were losing almost 2.1% in value this afternoon while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was declining about 1.51%.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(-) Snap ( SNAP ) retreated to a record low on Friday, dropping over 17% to a worst-ever $5.77 a share after saying over 2 million users quit using the photo-sharing application during the July-to-September reporting period, marking the second quarter in a row the number of daily active users has declined. The 1.1% sequential drop to 186 million daily active users followed a 1.6% decline during the previous quarter and upstaged better-than-expected Q3 financial resuls. Excluding one-time items, its net loss shrank to $0.12 per share from $0.14 per share in the year-ago period and beating the Capital IQ consensus expecting a $0.14 per share net loss. Revenue increased 43% to $298 million, also surpassing the analyst mean by around $15 million. Also weighing on Snap shares Friday was a downgrade to underweight from neutral at J.P. Morgan, which also halved its price target for the stock to $6 a share.
In other sector news:
(+) Mellanox Technologies ( MLNX ) soared Friday, topping out with a nearly 18% advance, following reports it has hired an investment banker to assist with exploring a potential sale of the fabless chipmaker. The move follows the company receiving expressions of interest from at least two rivals, CNBC said, citing unnamed sources who also said the talks are still at an early stage and may not result in a transaction.
(+) National Instruments ( NATI ) climbed as much as 16% on Friday after analysts at Deutsche Bank raised their investment recommendation for the automation and measurement software firm to Buy From Hold and also increased their price target for the company's stock by $5 to $50 a share. The upgrade follows National Instruments late Thursday reporting non-GAAP Q3 net income of $0.45 per share on $346.1 million in revenue, exceeding the Capital IQ consensus by $0.07 per share and $3.4 million, respectively.
(-) Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL) at one point slid almost 6% lower on Friday after missing analyst estimates with its Q3 revenue. Total revenue rose 22% year over year to $33.74 billion but still lagged the Capital IQ consensus by around $260 million. The internet conglomerate earned $13.06 per share during the three months ended Sept. 30, improving on a $9.57 per share profit last year and beating the Street view by $2.65 per share.
